t: Read and write standard cube notation: R, U', F2, wide moves, slices, rotations
desc: Learn the six face letters (U D L R F B), prime and double turns, lowercase/w wide moves, the M E S slices and x y z rotations, then execute 3 written scrambles on a solved cube.
check: What exactly does R' do, and from which viewpoint is its direction judged?
How does r (or Rw) differ from R, and which face does M follow in direction?
What do the rotations x, y and z do, and which face turn does each follow?
a: R' turns the right face 90 degrees counterclockwise, judged as if you were looking straight at the right face.
r/Rw turns the right face plus the middle slice together; R turns only the outer face. M turns in the same direction as L.
They turn the whole cube without moving pieces relative to each other: x follows R, y follows U, z follows F.

t: Solve the first layer: white cross plus all four white corners
desc: Build a white cross whose edges also match the side centres, then put each white corner above its slot and repeat R U R' U' until it drops in correctly oriented. Practise on fresh scrambles.
check: First layer completed on 5 different scrambles without a guide
Every cross edge matches its side centre (a coloured 'T' on each side)
All four first-layer corners correctly placed and oriented on each attempt

t: Finish your first complete solve with the beginner layer-by-layer method
desc: After the first layer: insert middle edges (U R U' R' U' F' U F or its mirror), make the yellow cross (F R U R' U' F'), orient corners with Sune (R U R' U R U2 R'), then permute corners and edges.
check: One full solve completed using your notes
Three full solves completed from memory with no notes
Every algorithm used written out correctly from memory

t: Drill the Sune and Anti-Sune until both are automatic
desc: Sune is R U R' U R U2 R'; Anti-Sune is R U2 R' U' R U' R' (they are inverses). Set up each case by doing the other algorithm, then recognise and solve it on sight. Repeat 20 times each.
check: Each algorithm executed 10 times in a row with no mistakes
Sune executed in under 2 seconds
Correct algorithm chosen from the top-layer pattern 5 out of 5 times

t: Learn 2-look PLL: 2 corner algorithms and 4 edge algorithms
desc: Corners first: headlights on one side -> T-perm, no headlights -> Y-perm. Then edges: Ua, Ub, H and Z perms. Drill recognition on random last layers before chasing speed.
check: All 6 algorithms performed from memory
Correct case recognised 10 out of 10 times
Permutation step finished in under 20 seconds on 5 consecutive solves

t: Learn 2-look OLL: 3 edge cases and 7 corner cases
desc: Edges: line -> F R U R' U' F'; L shape -> f R U R' U' f'; dot -> do both. Corners: Sune, Anti-Sune, H, Pi, Headlights (U), T and L (bowtie). Learn one case at a time, drilling each 10 times.
check: All 10 algorithms performed from memory
Top face completed in two looks on 10 scrambles in a row
Each of the 7 corner cases named on sight within 2 seconds

t: Understand intuitive F2L: pairing a corner and edge without algorithms
desc: Learn why F2L replaces separate corner and middle-edge steps: pair each first-layer corner with its edge in the top layer, then insert with triggers like R U R' or R U' R'. Experiment slowly on a solved cross.
check: Which two pieces make an F2L 'pair', and where do they end up?
Why does a trigger like R U R' leave the cross intact?
What do you do if the corner is stuck in the wrong slot?
a: A first-layer corner and its matching middle-layer edge; together they fill one of the four slots between the cross and the top layer.
R moves the cross edge into the middle layer, U only turns the top layer so it can't touch it, and R' puts it straight back.
Take it out with a trigger (e.g. R U R') so it lands in the top layer, then pair it with its edge and insert normally.

t: Complete cross plus intuitive F2L on 5 scrambles with no algorithm sheet
desc: Solve the cross then all four F2L pairs on 5 scrambles, working out each pair by hand. Count moves per pair and redo any pair that took more than 15 moves until you find a shorter way.
check: Cross plus 4 pairs completed on 5 scrambles
No pair needed more than 15 moves on the last 2 scrambles
Cross still intact after the final pair every time

t: Plan your whole cross during the 15-second inspection
desc: Scramble, inspect for 15 seconds and plan every cross move, then execute without pausing (try eyes closed). Any cross can be solved in 8 moves or fewer, so aim for that.
check: Cross executed without pausing on 7 of 10 scrambles
Cross correct with eyes closed on at least 3 of 10
Average cross length of 8 moves or fewer

t: Finger-trick the sexy move: 6 reps of R U R' U' in under 3 seconds
desc: From home grip: R with the right wrist, U with a right index flick, R' with the wrist, U' with a left index flick. Six repetitions return the cube to solved, so the drill checks itself.
check: 6 reps return the cube to solved
6 reps completed in under 3 seconds
No regrips during the 6 reps

t: Learn 6 more PLLs: Aa, Ab, Ja, Jb, Ra and F perm
desc: Pick one algorithm source and learn these one at a time, including recognition from two sides (headlights, blocks, bars). Added to T, Y, Ua, Ub, H and Z, you will know 12 of the 21 PLLs.
check: All 6 new algorithms performed from memory
Each case recognised correctly from at least 2 angles
Each new algorithm executed in under 3 seconds

t: Understand the Roux method: blocks, CMLL and the last six edges
desc: Learn Roux's four steps: build a 1x2x3 block on the left, another on the right, solve the top corners (CMLL), then the last six edges (LSE) with only M and U moves. Try building a first block slowly.
check: What are the four steps of Roux, in order?
Why can LSE use only M and U moves?
Why does Roux usually need fewer moves than CFOP?
a: First block (left 1x2x3), second block (right 1x2x3), CMLL (top corners), LSE (last six edges).
M and U never disturb the two 1x2x3 blocks, and U only shifts the solved corners together, fixed by a final U turn.
Blocks are built intuitively without preserving a cross, and LSE is very efficient; good Roux solves are often under 50 moves.

t: Build both Roux blocks on 10 scrambles
desc: On 10 scrambles, build the left 1x2x3 block, then the right one using mostly R, r, U and M moves so the first block is untouched. Finish with any last layer method or just rescramble.
check: Both blocks built on 10 scrambles
First block in 12 moves or fewer on at least 3 scrambles
Second block built without breaking the first every time

t: Solve a 2x2 cube using 3x3 algorithms you already know
desc: Build one full layer whose side colours match each other (there are no centres), then orient the top with your corner OLLs (Sune etc.) and swap corners with a T-perm or Y-perm.
check: 5 solves completed without help
Average of 5 under 40 seconds
First layer correct every time (side colours match), not just one face

t: Solve a Pyraminx: tips, centres, first layer, last three edges
desc: Twist the four tips to match, align the three-colour centre pieces, solve one face with its three edges, then learn a single 3-edge-cycle algorithm to finish the last layer.
check: 5 solves completed without notes
Average of 5 under 60 seconds
Tips solved during inspection on every solve

t: Why some cube states are impossible: piece counts and invariants
desc: Learn how many positions a 3x3 has, why a single flipped edge or twisted corner can never come from turning, and what God's number means. Try to explain each to a friend.
check: Roughly how many positions does a 3x3 Rubik's Cube have?
Why can't a legally turned cube have exactly one twisted corner?
What is God's number for the 3x3 and what does it mean?
a: Every legal move keeps total corner twist at 0 (mod 3), so one twisted corner means the cube was taken apart or twisted by hand.
20: every position can be solved in 20 moves or fewer (half-turn metric), proved by computer in 2010.

t: Blindfolded basics: Old Pochmann for edges and letter-pair memo
desc: Learn Old Pochmann edges: letter every sticker (Speffz scheme), trace targets from the buffer, then solve each with a setup move, a T-perm and the exact undo of the setup.
check: In Old Pochmann edges, which positions does the T-perm swap?
What rule must setup moves follow?
What do you do when the buffer piece returns to the buffer before all edges are solved?
a: The buffer at UR with the swap position UL (it also swaps two corners, which cancel out with an even number of targets).
Only bring the target to UL without disturbing UR, then undo them in exact reverse after the T-perm.
That is a cycle break: shoot to any unsolved edge to start a new cycle and keep tracing from there.

t: Solve all 12 edges of a 3x3 blindfolded with Old Pochmann
desc: Scramble, memorise only the edge targets as letter pairs, put on a blindfold (or close your eyes) and execute. Check the result, find the mistake, and repeat for 3 attempts.
check: Edge memo completed in under 5 minutes
At least 1 of 3 attempts with every edge solved
Cause identified for each failed attempt (memo, setup or execution)

t: Understand speedcubing averages and inspection rules, then compute yours
desc: Learn how WCA-style ao5 and ao12 are computed and how inspection penalties work, then do 12 timed solves and calculate both averages by hand.
check: How is an average of 5 (ao5) calculated?
Why are the best and worst times dropped?
How long is WCA inspection and what happens if you go over?
a: Drop the single best and single worst of 5 times and take the mean of the middle 3. An ao12 drops best and worst and averages 10.
So one lucky scramble or one disaster doesn't distort the number; it reflects your typical speed.
15 seconds. Starting after 15 s but before 17 s gives a +2 penalty; starting after 17 s is a DNF.

t: Train lookahead: 10 slow solves with pause-free F2L
desc: Do 10 solves turning at roughly half speed while finding the next F2L pair during the current insertion. A metronome at 1-2 turns per second helps keep the pace steady.
check: 10 solves with no F2L pause longer than 1 second
Next pair located before the current one is inserted on most pairs
Average within 10 seconds of your normal average despite slower turning
